Muslim Companion for Alexa

The Athan at your local prayer times, adhkar after the prayer, Quran recitation and reminders from your masjid, on your Amazon Echo.
✔ Live on Alexa
Open DashboardTry Web App

How It Works

Set up your personal muezzin in three simple steps — it takes less than five minutes.

Enable the Skill

Open the Alexa app on your phone, search for Muslim Companion, and tap Enable to Use. Then say “Alexa, open Muslim Companion” to confirm.

Sign In & Configure

Visit alexa.imuslimlife.com, sign in, confirm your location, choose your Athan voice, and follow your masjid (for example AMCC) for iqamah and Jumu'ah reminders.

Or by voice: “Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set my calculation method to ISNA” and “…to set my madhab to Hanafi”, no dashboard needed. See the voice commands below.

Create a Routine & Enjoy

In the Alexa app, create one routine: when the Muslim Companion Azan sensor opens, open Muslim Companion. Your Echo then plays the Athan automatically at every prayer time. Our step-by-step setup guide walks you through it with screenshots.

See it in action

Set up Muslim Companion in under a minute

Once the routine is saved, finish your setup: sign in at alexa.imuslimlife.com, or open the Salat-e-Mustaqeem app and tap the Alexa icon.

Open the dashboard

Key Features

Everything is set up at alexa.imuslimlife.com, and every extra is off until you turn it on
🔊

Athan at your prayer times

Your Echo plays the Athan at your local times for all five prayers, with a choice of Athan voices and a special Fajr Athan.

🕌

Masjid Connect

Follow your masjid (like AMCC) and get a reminder before each iqamah and before Jumu'ah, with the times your masjid publishes.

📖

Quran recitation

More than 30 renowned reciters. One surah after the Athan, or keep the Quran playing through the day, and pick up where you left off.

📿

Adhkar after the prayer

Ayat al-Kursi and the three Quls after each prayer, with Arabic text and English or Urdu translation. Off until you turn it on.

🎓

Hifz Coach

Memorize a few ayahs at a time on your Echo: each ayah three times, then the whole lesson together, with your progress saved. Practice online too.

🌙

Ramadan mode

A Suhoor reminder before Fajr, Iftar announced at Maghrib, and Makkah Taraweeh recitation after Isha.

📺

Echo Show screen

Today's prayer times on screen with the next prayer highlighted and a countdown, plus an always-on Prayer Times widget.

💡

Home Scenes

Dim the lights at the Athan, wake gently before Fajr, or set a calm evening after Isha, using your own Alexa routines.

🤲

Duas after the Athan

The Dua after the Athan and the Duas you choose, played on your Echo right after the Athan.

🧭

Qibla direction

Ask which way is the Qibla: the direction from your home in degrees and as a compass point, and how far Makkah is.

🗓️

Hijri date & Islamic calendar

Today's Hijri date, and how many days until Ramadan, Eid, Ashura, Arafah or the white days. The same dates as your prayer times.

🍽️

Sunnah fasting

Ask when the next Sunnah fast is, or get a reminder after Isha the evening before Mondays, Thursdays, the white days, Arafah and Ashura.

📿

Tasbih & morning and evening adhkar

Alexa counts dhikr with you (33, 33, 34 after the prayer), with a tap counter on Echo Show, and plays the morning and evening adhkar.

🌐

Quran with translation

Play any surah by voice, with English or Urdu after each ayah, and Surah Al-Kahf every Friday.

✨

Daily Dua, Hadith & Names of Allah
Coming soon: scholar review

A short dua, hadith or one of the 99 Names each day, with its source, reviewed by a scholar before it is published.

See it in action

Real screens for a family that follows AMCC in Florida: prayer times for their own location, iqamah times published by the masjid.
On your Echo Show

Say “Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for today’s prayer times”: the five prayers and sunrise, your masjid’s iqamah next to each one, and the next prayer highlighted with a countdown.

On your phone

At alexa.imuslimlife.com, open My Masjid and choose your masjid. You see today’s athan and iqamah times and this Friday’s Jumu’ah, and you choose when your Echo reminds you before the iqamah and Jumu’ah.

Always-on widget

On Echo Show 8, 10 and 15, add the Prayer Times widget: the next prayer, its countdown and your masjid’s iqamah stay on the home screen.

Coming soon

Eight new widgets for Echo Show

Choose the look you love for your home screen. These widgets are with Amazon for review and will appear in your Echo Show's widget gallery once they're approved.

Mihrab window

The next prayer framed in an arched window, with its countdown.

Sun arc

The sun travels across the day from Fajr to Isha, so you see where you are at a glance.

Five lamps

One lamp for each prayer; the next prayer's lamp glows gold.

Illuminated page

The next prayer in gold Arabic calligraphy on a warm, manuscript-style page.

Printed timetable

All five prayers in a clean printed table, with the next one marked.

Ink arch

An ink-drawn arch around the next prayer and its countdown.

Ayah of the Day

A new ayah every day in Arabic with its English meaning (Saheeh International).

Now Reciting

The surah and reciter playing on your Echo, right on the home screen.

Mushaf read-along

Also in review: follow the recitation on a Mushaf page on your Echo Show, with each word highlighted as it is recited. Tap a word to jump to that ayah.

Voice Commands

Everything you can say to Muslim Companion, grouped by feature. Using an AI assistant? Connect it to our prayer times.
Languages and countries

Muslim Companion understands English, Arabic (“الرفيق المسلم”) and Hindi (“मुस्लिम कम्पैनियन”). In English, say the phrases exactly as written, starting with “Alexa, ask Muslim Companion…” (the name is the same in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, India and Australia). Choose a language above to see the Arabic or Hindi phrases. Where a phrase has a choice, such as a calculation method, the description lists every option you can say.

Commands marked Coming soon are not available yet; the badge says why.

Getting started

Prayer times

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what is my next prayer”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is the next prayer”

Says the next prayer, its time and how long until it, plus your masjid's iqamah if you follow one.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is Maghrib”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what time is Fajr”

Says the time for one prayer today (after Isha, Fajr is tomorrow's).

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for today's prayer times”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for prayer times”

Reads all of today's times. On an Echo Show it also shows them on screen with the next prayer and a countdown.

Shows on Echo Show

Location

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to use my Echo's location”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to update my location”

Sets your prayer times from your Echo's address (after you allow Device Address in the Alexa app). Only the city and approximate coordinates are kept.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for prayer times where I am”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for prayer times near me”

In the Alexa app on your phone: prayer times where you are right now, for that answer only. Your Athans at home don't change.

“Yes”
“No”

Answers a question from Muslim Companion, such as whether to use your Echo's location.

While Muslim Companion is playing

Your prayer settings

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to read my prayer settings”

Says your location, calculation method and Asr madhab, and how to change them.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set my calculation method to Umm al-Qura”
“Alexa, tell Muslim Companion to use the Muslim World League method”
“Alexa, tell Muslim Companion my masjid uses ISNA”

Changes how your prayer times are calculated: ISNA, Muslim World League, Umm al-Qura, Egyptian, Karachi, Gulf, Kuwait, Qatar, Singapore, France, Turkey, Russia, Tehran or Jafari. Alexa confirms with your new next prayer time and tells you how to go back.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set my madhab to Hanafi”
“Alexa, tell Muslim Companion I follow the Hanafi madhab”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set my madhab to standard”

Sets the Asr time: Hanafi (later Asr), or standard for Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion which calculation method should I use”

Suggests the method most used where you live (for example ISNA in North America, Turkey's Diyanet in Turkey) and offers to switch: say yes or no.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what calculation method am I using”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what is my madhab”

Other ways to ask for your settings.

Tip: No dashboard needed: set how your prayer times are calculated by voice. Your Athans move to the new times right away.

Athan

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play athan”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play athan in Makkah”

Plays the Athan now, with the Duas and Quran you chose after it. Voices you can name include Makkah, Madinah, Mishary and Zahrani.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play fajr athan”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play maghrib athan”

Plays that prayer's Athan (Fajr uses its own Athan voice).

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to test athan”

Plays the Athan once so you can check the sound on this Echo.

Automatic Athan

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what is my scheduled athan status”

Tells you whether the automatic Athan is on.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to enable scheduled athan”

Turns the automatic Athan on. It plays at each prayer time through your Alexa routine (see the Setup Guide).

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to disable scheduled athan”

Turns the automatic Athan off for all prayers until you turn it on again.

Turns the automatic Athan off

Quran and playback

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play Surah Al-Kahf”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play Surah Baqarah by Qari Badar”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play Fatiha by Maher”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play surah number 36”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play Surah Yasin with English translation”

Plays any surah by name or number, said the way you say it (Fatiha or Fateha, Baqarah or Surah Baqara, Nisa…), with your reciter or the one you name (Qari Badar, Maher, Al-Muaiqly, Sudais…), or with an English or Urdu translation after each ayah.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion which reciters do you have”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion which reciters start with S”

Lists the reciters, or the ones whose name starts with a letter. If Alexa doesn't know a reciter you name, it suggests the ones starting with the same letter.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn on Friday Kahf”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn off Friday Kahf”

Every Friday, Surah Al-Kahf plays after the Fajr Athan (or Dhuhr, set on the dashboard).

“Alexa, next”
“Alexa, previous”

While the Quran plays: the next or previous surah. During the Athan and Duas, Next skips ahead.

While Muslim Companion is playing
“Alexa, start over”

Starts the current surah again.

While Muslim Companion is playing
“Alexa, pause”
“Alexa, resume”

Pauses the recitation and carries on from the same place.

While Muslim Companion is playing
“Alexa, stop”
“Alexa, cancel”

Stops the Athan or recitation at any time.

While Muslim Companion is playing
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion how far am I in the Quran”

Tells you your Quran Journey: listening time and how much of the khatm you have heard.

“Alexa, shuffle”
“Alexa, loop”

Explains how to choose Random or continuous Quran on the Quran Schedule page.

While Muslim Companion is playing
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to read along Surah Al-Kahf”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to open mushaf page 293”

On an Echo Show 8 or larger, shows the Madinah mushaf page by page in tajweed colours while Maher Al-Muaiqly recites. The verse being recited is lit up, the page turns by itself, and you can tap a verse to recite from there. Say next page, previous page, pause or resume. The Echo Show 15 adds the translation beside the page.

Mushaf read-along is being tested on Echo Show.
Shows on Echo Show

Hifz Coach

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to start Hifz”

Plays your current lesson: each ayah repeated, then the whole lesson together. On an Echo Show the ayah appears on screen.

Shows on Echo Show
“Alexa, tell Muslim Companion I memorized it”

Marks the lesson memorized and moves to the next one.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to repeat each ayah five times”

Sets how many times each ayah repeats: 1, 3, 5, 7 or 10.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion how is my Hifz”

Tells you how many ayahs you have memorized and your current lesson.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to link my phone”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to link my phone with code 123456”

Links this Echo to your Salat-e-Mustaqeem phone account with the six-digit code from the app (More, then Alexa), so your Hifz progress shows on the phone.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn tajweed colours on”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn tajweed colours off”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set tajweed to full”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to set tajweed to soft”

Turns the tajweed colours on your Hifz lesson on or off, or sets them to soft or full. On an Echo Show the lesson screen redraws at once.

Tajweed colours by voice is being tested.
Shows on Echo Show

Tip: During a lesson, "Alexa, next" and "Alexa, previous" move by ayah, and "Alexa, start over" repeats the ayah.

My Masjid

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is iqamah”

Says the next iqamah time at the masjid you follow.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is jumuah”

Says this week's Jumu'ah time or times at your masjid.

Ramadan

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn on Ramadan mode”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn off Ramadan mode”

Turns Ramadan mode on or off: Suhoor reminder, Iftar at Maghrib and Taraweeh recitation after Isha.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion is Ramadan mode on”

Tells you whether Ramadan mode is on.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is suhoor”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is iftar”

Says when Suhoor ends (Fajr) and when Iftar is (Maghrib).

Qibla and the Islamic calendar

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion which way is the Qibla”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion where is the Qibla”

Says the Qibla direction from your saved location in degrees from true north and as a compass point, and how far Makkah is.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what is the Hijri date”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion what is the Islamic date today”

Says today's Hijri date (the same date as the app and your Echo Show), and if today is a special day.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is Ramadan”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion how many days until Eid”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when are the white days”

When Ramadan, Eid, Ashura, Arafah, the Islamic New Year, the last ten nights or the white days are, with a countdown. Dates follow Umm al-Qura and can differ by a day where the moon is sighted locally.

Sunnah fasting

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion when is the next Sunnah fast”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion should I fast tomorrow”

The next Sunnah fast: Mondays and Thursdays, the white days, Arafah, Ashura and the six days of Shawwal.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn on fasting reminders”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn off fasting reminders”

A reminder after Isha on the evening before a Sunnah fast, through your Muslim Companion routine.

Adhkar, Tasbih and daily reminders

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play the morning adhkar”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to play the evening adhkar”

Ayat al-Kursi, then Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas three times each, recited.

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn on morning and evening adhkar”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to turn off evening adhkar”

Plays the morning adhkar after Fajr and the evening adhkar after Asr every day (or Maghrib, set on the dashboard).

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to start tasbih”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion to count 33 subhanallah”

Counts dhikr with you at a gentle pace. With no dhikr named, it leads the tasbih after the prayer: 33 SubhanAllah, 33 Alhamdulillah and 34 Allahu Akbar. On an Echo Show, tap the screen to count.

Shows on Echo Show
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for today's dua”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for today's hadith”
“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for the name of allah of the day”

A short daily dua, hadith or Name of Allah with its source, reviewed by a scholar before it is published.

Getting started

“Alexa, open Muslim Companion”

Starts the skill (it plays the Athan for the current prayer).

“Alexa, ask Muslim Companion for help”

Lists what you can ask.

You can also start with “Alexa, open Muslim Companion” and then ask. Commands like “next”, “pause” and “stop” work while Muslim Companion is playing.

Common Questions

Which Alexa devices does this skill work with?

The Muslim Companion skill works with any Amazon Echo device or Alexa-enabled device. For the best audio experience, we recommend devices with quality speakers such as the Echo, Echo Dot, or Echo Show.

Does the skill automatically adjust for daylight saving time?

Yes, the skill automatically adjusts prayer times based on your location's time zone and daylight saving time changes. You'll always get accurate prayer times without having to make any manual adjustments.

Can I customize which prayers play the athan?

Absolutely! You can choose which prayer times should play the athan. For example, you might want to enable it only for Fajr, Maghrib and Isha, or for all five daily prayers. You choose this on the Prayer Settings page at alexa.imuslimlife.com.

Is there a cost to use this skill?

The Muslim Companion skill is completely free. The core functionality — accurate prayer times and automated athan — remains free for the Muslim community, always.

What if my internet connection goes down?

Your prayer times are calculated in advance, but your Echo needs an internet connection to play the Athan. If your connection is down at prayer time, that Athan may be missed; everything resumes automatically once you are back online.
